title: Your first breakpoint
summary: Freeze the program on a line and look at every variable.

say.never: A **debugger** lets you pause a running program on any line you choose, like pausing a video. While it's paused you can see the value of every variable. Then you move forward one line at a time and watch what changes.
say.bit: A debugger pauses the program on a line you pick, so you can look at every variable and move one line at a time.

marks.label: a breakpoint here pauses every time round

say.never: A **breakpoint** is where the program pauses. Click in the narrow space just **left of a line number** and a **red dot** appears. When the program reaches that line, it stops *before* running it. Click the dot again to remove it.
say.bit: Click left of a line number for a red dot: the program stops before running that line.

marks.label: the breakpoint: click left of the line number

say.never: Breakpoints only work when you start the program with **Debug** instead of Run. Above `public static void main` there's a tiny **Run | Debug**: click **Debug**. Or click the little arrow next to ▷ at the top right and pick **Debug Java**.
say.bit: Start with **Debug** (above `main`, or the arrow next to ▷), not Run.

say.never: While the program is paused, a small toolbar appears at the top. **Continue** (▷) runs until the next breakpoint. **Step Over** (a curved arrow) runs just one line. **Stop** (the red square) ends it. Use these buttons, not the F-keys: in a browser, F5 reloads the page.
say.bit: Continue runs to the next stop, Step Over runs one line, Stop ends it. Use the buttons, not F-keys.

board.code: ▷ Continue   ↷ Step Over   ↓ Step Into   ↑ Step Out   ⟲ Restart   ■ Stop

say.never: On the left, the **Run and Debug** panel opens with a **Variables** list: every variable that exists right now, and its value. You can also rest the mouse on a variable in the code to see its value.
say.bit: The Variables list (left) shows every variable's value right now; hovering works too.
